author: product-requirements-expert
title: Reader narrows the veterinarian directory to one specialty
summary: Both the veterinarian directory page and its machine-readable form accept an optional specialty named in the request address, and list only the veterinarians holding it. The machine-readable form is a supported surface again.
acceptance_criteria: given the clinic's veterinarians, when the machine-readable form is requested, then it carries each veterinarian with the specialties they hold
given a specialty some veterinarians hold, when either form is narrowed to it, then only those veterinarians appear
given a specialty named in a different letter case than the stored one, when either form is narrowed to it, then it matches
given only the opening letters of a specialty's name, when either form is narrowed to it, then no veterinarian matches
given a specialty no veterinarian holds, when either form is narrowed to it, then the result is returned as usual with no veterinarian in it
given a specialty named as nothing or as spaces alone, when either form is requested, then every veterinarian appears
given no specialty is named, when either form is requested, then every veterinarian appears
given a narrowed directory spanning more than one page, when the next page is followed, then the narrowing still applies
edge case 3: given a specialty named with leading or trailing spaces, when either form is narrowed to it, then no veterinarian matches
non_goals: a form, dropdown, or any other page control for choosing the specialty
narrowing either form by any attribute other than specialty
narrowing the owner or pet listings
notes: NG-9 narrowed by owner decision; recorded in docs/adr/2026-08-30-non-goal-veterinarian-search-narrowed.md. The ADR index table in docs/adr/README.md still needs its row - that file is outside the product-requirements-expert write scope. REQ-VET-002 stays withdrawn and its id is not reused; the Superseded entry now reconciles with the reinstatement. Two residual choices are recorded in Open Questions: a visible control, and whether a specialty is matched after surrounding spaces are dropped. Edge case 3 states the narrowest reading until that is settled.

scope_overrides.owner_decision: Non-goal NG-9 is narrowed: free-text veterinarian search stays out of scope, but filtering the directory by an attribute it already shows is in. Record the narrowing the way the project records non-goal changes.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Narrowing a paged listing by a request parameter is the owner-search shape applied to the vet package. No new pattern, module, or dependency. The project has no service layer (ADR 2026-07-31-feature-package-organization), so the predicate belongs on VetRepository as a Spring Data derived query and the controller only decides whether to apply it. Mirror the existing findAll pair: add an unpaged Collection-returning overload for /vets and a Page-returning overload for /vets.html, so both surfaces share one predicate declaration rather than two. Recommended names: findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String) and findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase(String, Pageable); the path traverses Vet.specialties to Specialty's inherited NamedEntity.name. IgnoreCase compiles to upper(...) = upper(...) in JPQL, which is vendor-independent and therefore does not repeat the PostgreSQL collation defect that Known Defects records for owner search. Filtering in the controller over findAll() is rejected: it would make totalPages and totalElements describe the unfiltered set and duplicate the predicate across the two routes. docs/system-design.md updated: the Known Defects row calling the machine-readable route pending removal is deleted (it contradicted the ADR and the PRD Superseded entry), and Vets, VetRepository, VetController now cite REQ-VET-003. docs/adr/README.md gained the index row for 2026-08-30-non-goal-veterinarian-search-narrowed.md.
integration_points: VetController.showVetList gains @RequestParam(required = false) String specialty; the blank decision lives in one private helper both routes call, so /vets.html and /vets cannot drift on what blank means
VetController.showResourcesVetList gains the same parameter and calls the unpaged overload; Vets stays an unchanged serialization wrapper
VetController.addPaginationModel puts the specialty on the model as null when absent, so the template omits the parameter rather than emitting an empty one
vetList.html: all six paging anchors must carry the specialty; no form, dropdown, or other control is added to the page
VetRepository gains the two filtered overloads alongside the existing findAll pair; no other package references them

patterns.description: findByLastNameStartingWith(String, Pageable) - the repository owns both the predicate and the paging; copy the shape, not the StartingWith keyword (this slice matches the whole name)
controller normalizes the request parameter, then branches to the broad or narrow query; copy the branch, NOT the strip() at line 103 - see risks
the findAll() / findAll(Pageable) overload pair the filtered methods mirror
@DataJpaTest already injecting VetRepository against seeded H2 data - the home for the derived-query semantics assertions

risks.risk: The vets cache is created with no size limit or eviction (CacheConfiguration, and Open Questions item 5). Annotating the filtered methods @Cacheable("vets") makes an anonymous caller the author of cache keys: every distinct query string mints an entry that is never evicted. Unbounded growth reachable without authentication.
risks.mitigation: Leave the two filtered methods uncached. The cache exists for the unfiltered directory; the narrowed query goes to the database each time. Note the reason at the method so a later reader does not add the annotation for symmetry.

risks.risk: Copying OwnerController's lastName.strip() would silently resolve the open question the PRD deliberately left open: edge case 3 requires that a value with leading or trailing spaces is matched as given and therefore matches nothing.
risks.mitigation: Blank-test with isBlank() (spaces alone means no specialty was named), and pass any non-blank value to the repository unstripped.

risks.risk: specialties.name carries an index, not a unique constraint. If two specialty rows shared a name, an inner join over vet_specialties would return a vet twice and inflate totalElements.
risks.mitigation: Use the Distinct keyword in the derived query name; Spring Data applies count(distinct ...) to the matching count query.

risks.risk: vetList.html builds hrefs by string concatenation ('/vets.html?page=__${i}__'). Concatenating a request-derived specialty into that produces an unencoded value in the URL, and a value containing & or # breaks or rewrites the link.
risks.mitigation: Switch the six anchors to Thymeleaf's URL-parameter form, @{/vets.html(page=${...}, specialty=${specialty})}. It URL-encodes each parameter and omits one whose value is null, which also gives the absent-parameter case for free. This is the security-principles cross-site-scripting row applied to an href.

risks.risk: VetControllerTests is a @WebMvcTest with a @MockitoBean VetRepository. Three acceptance criteria - case-insensitive match, no partial match, and empty result on an unheld specialty - are properties of the derived query, and a stubbed repository proves none of them.
risks.mitigation: Assert the query semantics in ClinicServiceTests (@DataJpaTest, real H2, seeded radiology/surgery/dentistry rows). Keep VetControllerTests for the controller's own behavior: parameter binding, the blank branch, the model attribute, and the paging links.

notes: Address contract is fixed by the prd-entry and not the design stage's to move: /vets.html?specialty=<name> and /vets?specialty=<name>, parameter named exactly specialty. Absent parameter must leave today's behavior byte-identical - route the absent and blank cases to the existing findAll methods rather than passing a wildcard to the filtered one. A specialty no vet holds returns HTTP 200 with an empty list, not 404; the empty page renders the table with no rows, which the existing template already does. Vet.specialties is FetchType.EAGER, so the filtered page query yields the join for the predicate and Hibernate loads each vet's specialties separately - the rendered row still shows every specialty a matched vet holds, which is what edge case 2 requires. Durable memory written this dispatch: docs/adr/README.md index row added; docs/system-design.md Known Defects row for the machine-readable route removed and three vet Contracts rows now cite REQ-VET-003. Left for doc-sync after the code lands: nothing in the Contracts table, since the purpose columns already describe both routes. Two PRD Open Questions stay open and must not be closed by implementation choice - a visible control for the narrowing, and whether surrounding spaces are dropped before matching. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log; the audit step is a no-op.

author: review-plan-engine
rationale: risk triggers present (multi-module, oversize, design-revision); full battery

author: code-quality-reviewer
approved_aspects: VetRepository's two filtered overloads carry Javadoc explaining both the matching semantics (whole-name, case-insensitive) and the deliberate absence of @Cacheable, so a later reader does not add caching for symmetry with findAll
VetController centralizes the blank/absent decision in one private namesASpecialty helper that both routes call, avoiding drift between /vets and /vets.html on what an unnamed specialty means
namesASpecialty is a pure predicate (no side effects) named and used consistently with query-method conventions

vetList.html's paging anchors use Thymeleaf's @{...} parameter form (URL-encoded) with an explicit null-check ternary per anchor plus an HTML comment explaining why, rather than silently letting a null parameter render as specialty=
./gradlew checkFormat passes with no formatting violations

Naming (findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase, namesASpecialty) follows existing repository/controller conventions and Spring Data naming rules; no get/set prefixes, no util/helper packages, no abbreviations

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Injection: the filter reaches the database only through the Spring Data derived query `findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase`, which binds the value as a JPA criteria parameter. No string-concatenated SQL or JPQL is introduced. The derived-query property path is resolved at context startup from the method name, not from request data, so no user-supplied value can steer it. Matches the SQL-injection row of the system-design threat model.

Reflected XSS on /vets.html: the value reaches the browser only through `th:href="@{/vets.html(page=...,specialty=${specialty})}"` on all six pagination links. The Thymeleaf link-expression parameter form URL-encodes the value and the attribute output is HTML-escaped by default in HTML template mode, so a payload such as `"><script>` renders inert as percent-encoded text. Swept the whole template set for the unescaped-output class (`th:utext`, `[(${...})]` unescaped inline, `th:onclick`, `javascript:` URLs) and found no instance anywhere under `src/main/resources/templates/`. VetControllerTests asserts the escaped `&` separator, which pins the escaping behaviour.

Model exposure: `specialty` is added to the model but rendered nowhere except the six href attributes; no other template reads the attribute. The controller normalizes an unnamed or blank value to null rather than echoing the raw value, which keeps the unnarrowed page's addresses byte-identical to the pre-change ones.

Cache-key authoring (the design's stated concern) holds as shipped: both new repository methods in VetRepository carry `@Transactional(readOnly = true)` and neither carries `@Cacheable("vets")`. Verified by reading the file, not the diff alone. An anonymous caller therefore cannot mint entries in the unbounded, evictionless `vets` cache.

Resource consumption from an unbounded-length or high-cardinality value: no amplification path found. Because the filtered lookups are uncached, a distinct value creates no retained server-side state; each request is one parameterized, paged (size 5) read against a bounded vets/specialties join, and the value's length is already capped by the container's request-line limit. Cost is bounded by the same factors as the pre-existing unfiltered route.

JSON route /vets: the value is consumed as a filter argument only and is never echoed into the response body, so the JSON surface adds no reflection sink. The response exposes no field the unfiltered route did not already expose.
Secrets: swept the production diff for credential-shaped names (token, password, secret, key, credential) and found none. No configuration, profile, or property file is touched by this change.

Supply chain: `build.gradle`, `settings.gradle`, `gradle.properties`, and the wrapper are untouched by the change set, so the slice introduces no new dependency, no new transitive surface, and no new CVE exposure to check against the NVD.

Attack surface delta: the change adds one optional read-only GET query parameter to two existing anonymous routes. It performs no write, no file I/O, no deserialization, no outbound call, and no privilege decision, so it crosses no trust boundary the application did not already cross. The absence of authentication on these routes is the pre-existing, documented posture recorded in the system-design Security Context, not a condition this slice introduces.

findings.description: VetRepository's Contracts row (line 103) still says 'results are cached' as a blanket claim, and Open Questions item 5 (line 218) still says 'the vet repository's read methods are cached with no eviction configured' as if this held for all of them. author: test-reviewer

findings.description: Edge case 2 ("a veterinarian holding several specialties appears under each of them") is untested for the narrowed query. Seeded vet Douglas (id 3) holds both surgery and dentistry, which is exactly the multi-specialty case the design block flagged as depending on Vet.specialties being FetchType.EAGER plus the Distinct keyword. None of the six new ClinicServiceTests methods filter by surgery or dentistry, and none assert on getSpecialties() of a matched vet -- only getLastName() is checked. A narrowing query could silently truncate a matched vet's specialty list (e.g. if a future refactor swapped the eager join for a projection) and no test would catch it.
findings.fix: Add theVetDirectoryShouldListEverySpecialtyOfAVetMatchedByOne(): call findDistinctBySpecialtiesNameIgnoreCase("surgery"), assert it contains Douglas and Ortega, and assert Douglas's getSpecialties() still contains both surgery and dentistry (extracting(Specialty::getName).containsExactlyInAnyOrder(...)) -- proving narrowing does not prune the returned vet's own specialty list.

findings.description: Three-Tier Data Naming (testing-principles.md § Three-Tier Data Naming Convention, which carries no grandfather clause for tests written from 2026-07-31 onward, unlike § Test Naming and § Factory Methods) is violated by every new test in both files. "radiology" is a Tier 1 meaningful value -- it directly determines the expected outcome (Leary/Stevens vs. empty) -- yet it appears as a bare string literal 12+ times across the two files with no role-describing name. Same for the expected vet surnames "Leary"/"Stevens" in the new ClinicServiceTests assertions.
findings.fix: Add a SEEDED_SPECIALTY = "radiology" (or similarly named) constant at class level in both ClinicServiceTests and VetControllerTests and reference it from every new test instead of the repeated literal; likewise name the expected-surname pair used in containsExactlyInAnyOrder.

findings.description: The "unheld specialty yields HTTP 200 with an empty list" acceptance bullet is exercised at the controller layer only incidentally: theVetDirectoryShouldPassTheSpecialtyToTheRepositoryUnstripped (html route) asserts status 200 and hasSize(0), but its stated purpose is proving the unstripped-value contract, not the unheld-specialty bullet, and there is no equivalent case for the JSON route (/vets). Confirm whether an explicit, purpose-named test for this bullet on both routes is required, or whether the incidental html coverage plus the ClinicServiceTests empty-result assertion (theVetDirectoryShouldListNoVetWhenNoVetHoldsTheNamedSpecialty) is accepted as sufficient.

approved_aspects: Mocking split holds as designed: ClinicServiceTests (@DataJpaTest, real H2) proves case-insensitivity, non-prefix matching, blank-vs-space semantics, and paging totals for the derived query; VetControllerTests (MockMvc + MockitoBean VetRepository, the file's pre-existing pattern) proves parameter binding, the blank branch, the model attribute, and that paging links carry or omit the specialty -- exactly the split the design block called for, and MockMvc is the one sanctioned controller-test mock per the brief.
New test names follow the brief's BDD school (the{Subject}Should{Outcome}) consistently.
Four-phase structure (Act+Assert separated from setup by a blank line, no phase comments) is followed in every new test.

theVetDirectoryShouldLeaveThePagingLinksUnnarrowedWhenNoSpecialtyIsNamed directly verifies the unnarrowed page's addresses stay free of the specialty parameter, matching the PRD's byte-identical-today requirement.
./gradlew test --tests ClinicServiceTests --tests VetControllerTests passes.

blast_radius.note: Nine files but one feature package: two repository overloads, one controller, one template, two test classes, four docs. The widest reach is the vetList.html rewrite of all six paging anchors, and that stays inside the one template the vet list already owns.

semantic_surprise.note: Every hunk does what the slice description says and no more. The blank decision is one isBlank helper both routes call; a non-blank value reaches the repository unstripped, which is the PRD's recorded edge case rather than a slip. The Distinct keyword guards the join against duplicate rows and the paged overload's totals describe the narrowed set. The rewritten anchors branch on a null specialty between two link expressions, so an unnarrowed page still renders /vets.html?page=2 exactly as before rather than a trailing specialty=. The filtered overloads carry no @Cacheable, which is deliberate and stated at the methods: a caller-named specialty would otherwise mint keys in a cache with no size limit and no eviction. That trade buys an uncached database read per narrowed request, bounded by page size on the HTML route and by the vets table on the JSON one.

test_adequacy.note: The tests exercise the changed behavior rather than restate it, and the split is right: the derived query's semantics are pinned in ClinicServiceTests against real seeded H2, so case-insensitivity, non-prefix matching, surrounding spaces, the empty result, the multi-specialty vet keeping its full specialty list, and the paging totals are all proven against the database rather than a stub. The controller tests assert the model attribute, the blank fall-through with a spaces-only value, and the rendered link content including the escaped ampersand, so a template regression that dropped or unencoded the parameter would fail. Each would fail against a plausibly broken implementation.
